entries.name: SWE-bench Verified
entries.summary: Fix real GitHub issues and check patches with repository tests.
entries.notes: Docker environments; agent system and model-only tracks differ.

entries.name: SWE-bench-Live
entries.summary: Evaluate coding agents on a continually refreshed collection of repository issues.
entries.notes: Use the same dated release and submission rules when comparing runs.

entries.name: LiveCodeBench
entries.summary: Test code generation on programming problems with explicit time windows.
entries.notes: Problem dates, model release dates and contamination flags matter.

entries.name: EvalPlus
entries.summary: Stress-test HumanEval and MBPP solutions with expanded test cases.
entries.notes: Keep prompt setting, greedy decoding and dataset versions fixed.

entries.name: BigCodeBench
entries.summary: Measure practical Python generation involving libraries and complex instructions.
entries.notes: Complete, Instruct, Full and Hard are distinct tracks; repository is archived.

entries.name: Terminal-Bench
entries.summary: Give agents executable tasks in real terminal environments.
entries.notes: Pin the benchmark release, agent harness and execution budget.

entries.name: SciCode
entries.summary: Evaluate scientific code generation with domain knowledge and execution tests.
entries.notes: Main problems and subproblems use different evaluation scopes.

entries.name: Aider Polyglot
entries.summary: Compare coding models through Aider across multiple programming languages.
entries.notes: Results depend on edit format, model settings and benchmark subset.

entries.name: Berkeley Function Calling
entries.summary: Check single-turn, multi-turn and agentic function calls.
entries.notes: Native function calling and prompted calls are separately declared.

entries.name: τ-bench
entries.summary: Evaluate customer-service agents on tool use, policy compliance and user interaction.
entries.notes: Current τ³ text, knowledge and voice tracks are separate from legacy τ².

entries.name: ToolSandbox
entries.summary: Test stateful tool use with intermediate milestones and conversational dependencies.
entries.notes: Run instructions and reference results live in the repository.

entries.name: WebArena
entries.summary: Complete realistic tasks on reproducible, self-hosted websites.
entries.notes: Website snapshots and browser agent settings must match.

entries.name: VisualWebArena
entries.summary: Solve web tasks requiring screenshots and visual reasoning.
entries.notes: This visual track differs from text-focused WebArena.

entries.name: WorkArena
entries.summary: Measure enterprise workflow automation in browser-based environments.
entries.notes: Hosted instance access and task configuration may be required.

entries.name: Mind2Web
entries.summary: Evaluate grounding and action prediction across diverse websites.
entries.notes: Offline action prediction and live web execution are different evaluations.

entries.name: OSWorld
entries.summary: Test computer-use agents on real desktop applications and files.
entries.notes: Execution requires isolated desktop environments; pin the release and step budget.

entries.name: GAIA
entries.summary: Challenge general assistants with research, tool use and multimodal questions.
entries.notes: Dataset access is gated; respect validation and hidden-test boundaries.

entries.name: MMLU-Pro
entries.summary: Evaluate broad knowledge and reasoning with more challenging multiple-choice questions.
entries.notes: Chain-of-thought and answer-extraction settings affect comparability.

entries.name: MMLU
entries.summary: Measure knowledge across academic and professional subjects.
entries.notes: Few-shot, zero-shot and prompt settings must be recorded.

entries.name: GPQA
entries.summary: Test graduate-level science reasoning on expert-authored questions.
entries.notes: GPQA Diamond is a specific subset; dataset access and terms apply.

entries.name: Humanity’s Last Exam
entries.summary: Evaluate difficult expert questions spanning science, mathematics and humanities.
entries.notes: Tool-assisted, no-tool, text-only and multimodal scores are separate settings.

entries.name: BIG-Bench Hard
entries.summary: Probe reasoning through challenging tasks selected from BIG-Bench.
entries.notes: Use a declared prompting protocol; this is not all of BIG-Bench.

entries.name: ARC-AGI-2
entries.summary: Solve novel grid transformations with strict separation between training and evaluation.
entries.metric: Solved tasks and cost per task
entries.notes: Base models, reasoning systems and competition systems use different constraints.

entries.name: ARC-AGI-3
entries.summary: Evaluate adaptation in novel interactive environments.
entries.notes: Interactive scoring and harness rules differ from ARC-AGI-1 and 2.

entries.name: GSM8K
entries.summary: Test multi-step grade-school mathematical word problems.
entries.notes: A useful baseline with substantial saturation and contamination risk.

entries.name: MATH
entries.summary: Evaluate competition-level mathematical problem solving.
entries.notes: Full MATH and MATH-500 are different test sets; dataset rights apply.

entries.name: MathArena
entries.summary: Compare reasoning models on dated mathematical competitions.
entries.notes: Competition year, inference budget and scoring policy are part of the result.

entries.name: MMMU
entries.summary: Test expert-level reasoning across images and academic disciplines.
entries.notes: Validation, test and Pro results must not be combined.

entries.name: MMMU-Pro
entries.summary: Use a harder visual reasoning track with stronger evaluation controls.
entries.notes: The Vision and Standard settings remain separate from original MMMU.

entries.name: MathVista
entries.summary: Combine visual perception and mathematical reasoning.
entries.notes: Keep test-mini and test evaluation splits separate.

entries.name: LongBench
entries.summary: Evaluate long-context understanding across tasks and languages.
entries.notes: Original LongBench and LongBench V2 use different tasks and metrics.

entries.name: RULER
entries.summary: Measure effective context length with controlled synthetic tasks.
entries.notes: Context size and task mix are essential to interpreting the score.

entries.name: IFEval
entries.summary: Check instruction-following constraints with deterministic verifiers.
entries.notes: Prompt-level and instruction-level scores use different denominators.

entries.name: HarmBench
entries.summary: Evaluate safety behavior against standardized harmful-behavior test cases.
entries.notes: Attack setup and grading policy determine the result; higher is not always better.

entries.name: TruthfulQA
entries.summary: Measure resistance to common falsehoods and misconceptions.
entries.notes: Generation and multiple-choice metrics are distinct.

entries.name: TextArena
entries.summary: Evaluate and train language-model agents in competitive and cooperative text games.
entries.notes: Each environment and multiplayer protocol defines its own comparison.

entries.name: LM Evaluation Harness
entries.summary: Run reproducible language-model evaluations across a large task library.
entries.notes: Choose model backend, dataset revision, prompt and seed; GPU or API costs are yours.

entries.name: Inspect AI
entries.summary: Build agent, tool-use and model evaluations with reusable scoring and sandboxes.
entries.notes: Includes an evaluation collection; external model calls and sandboxes need local setup.

entries.name: LightEval
entries.summary: Evaluate models using configurable tasks and multiple inference backends.
entries.notes: Record backend, model revision and generation settings.

entries.name: OpenCompass
entries.summary: Manage broad language-model evaluation with reusable model and dataset configurations.
entries.notes: Different datasets have different licensing and resource needs.

entries.name: HELM
entries.summary: Compare language models using explicit scenarios and multiple evaluation dimensions.
entries.notes: Accuracy, efficiency and other dimensions retain their separate meanings.

entries.name: VLMEvalKit
entries.summary: Run multimodal benchmarks through a common evaluation toolkit.
entries.notes: Dataset downloads, model access and judge settings vary.

entries.name: LMMS-Eval
entries.summary: Evaluate multimodal models across image, video and audio tasks.
entries.notes: Pin task configuration, dataset and model revision.

entries.name: BrowserGym
entries.summary: Run browser-agent tasks through a shared Gym-style environment.
entries.notes: An execution framework for web benchmarks, not a standalone universal ranking.

entries.name: Harbor
entries.summary: Run isolated agent evaluations and retain trial artifacts across benchmark environments.
entries.notes: Container execution and provider requests need explicit local configuration.

entries.name: Ragas
entries.summary: Evaluate retrieval, faithfulness and answer quality in RAG applications.
entries.notes: Judge-model configuration and your reference data affect the result.

entries.name: Promptfoo
entries.summary: Compare prompts, applications and agents with assertions and regression tests.
entries.notes: Run against your own providers and fixtures; judge-based checks incur model usage.

entries.name: DeepEval
entries.summary: Test LLM applications with configurable metrics and evaluation datasets.
entries.notes: Separate deterministic tests from model-graded evaluations.

entries.name: Garak
entries.summary: Probe model weaknesses with reproducible scanners and detectors.
entries.notes: Scope probes to systems you operate; detector results are not a universal safety score.

entries.name: OpenSpiel
entries.summary: Study competitive and cooperative agents across game environments and algorithms.
entries.notes: A research library for multi-agent games; bring an appropriate model adapter.
